Okay, we have work to do. I want to redesign everything from top to bottom. Here’s everything we’ll need to do, in roughly this order (if you think it should go differently, say so):
- Redesign home page
- Add start page
- Redesign case study format
- Add about page
- Remove articles (for now)

Here’s the the breakdown of the changes themselves:
- Home page now displays a preview of one case study at a time, with a row of large icons buttons across the top (below the top nav) for each
- When the user clicks on one of those icons, the page shifts to the new case study preview and the icon bar moves left or right to that case study (scrolling horizontally if the screen is too small to accommodate it)
- There’s also a pre-home page, the start page, that is what initially greets new visitors
- We now have an about page that includes a short intro to me, some quick facts about me, a breakdown of how I work, and my work history
- Articles are gone for now. I haven’t written anything new and the one that we currently have posted is in desperate need of a rewrite
- Case studies are now a much more guided experience, with distinct sections. The idea is that each is self-contained, though we can keep them on the same page if that’s the smartest way to structure it. I want there to be a snap to scroll though, where when you reach the end of a section (like the deep dive) there’s a sort of “hump” you have to get over and then it snaps to the top of the next section (in this case, the walkthrough). The buttons in the overview take the user directly to the marked section
- The overview of case studies is meant to be a presentation, larger than life. It should subtly animate in, utilizing motion.dev. We can start with something basic and then polish from there
- The deep dive is the write-up. We should reuse most of what we have, with some slight changes in max width and layout. The Problem, the Solution, and the Approach have been reordered, and the problem and solution are now combined (though they still use the same styling for their sections overall). The approach should keep it’s existing dotgrid background.
- I’ve used stand in still images in Figma, but the three detail sections should keep what they have in them for all three case studies, the text has just been restyled a bit
- The theme can be switched via the moon (in dark mode) or sun (in light mode)
- We’re displaying the user’s current date and time, live in the top right
- The icons in the far right of the top nav link to my GitHub, discord, and LinkedIn respectively
- We also have a new, persistent bottom nav with dynamic actions for the user depending on where they are. The start and about screens are the only places it doesn’t exist. These should be secondary buttons, with the styling laid out in a section within the Figma section I link to called New buttons. Make sure to pay close attention to what they do and their styling
- As part of that bottom nav and the new actions related to case studies, we need to add keyboard shortcut support. You’ll see icons on each of the buttons that tell the user what button on their keyboard corresponds to that action. We need to implement those
- There’s also a new side nav inside case studies and the about page that you should pay close attention to. It can have subsections within the nav that only expand when the user is in that section (like deep dive)
- For the map on the about page, I have an SVG we can use, but it would be cool to explore a real map that is a lofi dot matrix style. Let me know when you get to that and I’ll provide the SVG
- The list items in the work history use the same styling as the existing list on the home page and should link to their respective case studies 
- Just reuse the shadows we already have, don’t copy what’s in Figma for those
- All of this should use our existing design system, so modify tokens there as you need to. That way we get light and dark themes for free
- Buttons should depress on click. That means adjusting the shadows and scaling them down just slightly to get the effect. It may be as simple as the instructions in the attached screenshot, but you can also use motion.dev if it has anything helpful on that front
- Do your best on smaller screens and we can polish it after

# Portfolio redesign (v2.0): plan

## Context
Full top-to-bottom redesign of the portfolio (Astro 6 + React 19 islands + Tailwind v4, bun). Figma section "redesign" (file `yQsyiiyNzkw04y8TR6UCcK`, node `37:4587`) has these frames: Welcome (start), Home - Library, Case study - Ping (+ nav-on-scroll variant), Sub-nav, About, and a "New buttons" section. Goal: a guided, presentation-style experience with a persistent top nav (with live clock) and bottom action bar, keyboard shortcuts, and an About page.

## Findings that change the brief (please sanity-check)
1. **Astro, not a React SPA.** Routing is file-based (`src/pages`). Case studies are MDX in `src/content/projects/*.mdx`, rendered by `src/layouts/ProjectLayout.astro`.
2. **No top nav, clock, or icon theme toggle exists.** The theme toggle is a text button in `Footer.astro`. Theme = `.dark` class on `<html>` + `localStorage.theme`, with a view-transition sweep (reuse this logic).
3. **"Undercurrent" is not this repo's design system** (it's a case study with a scoped `--uc-demo-*` kit). The site's real tokens are `--portfolio-*` in `src/styles/global.css` (bg/ink/muted/accent, `--media-frame-shadow`, radii). **Plan assumption: extend `--portfolio-*` tokens in `global.css`** (light + dark come free). `ui/button.tsx` (shadcn) is unused; the real button is `PillButton.astro`.
4. Motion (`motion` ^12) is already installed and used (`src/lib/animations.ts`). No tests, no CLAUDE.md.
5. Figma variables are not bound (empty), so exact values come from design context/screenshots when building each piece. Button section specs (`64:5974`) get pulled at implementation time.

## Architecture decisions
- **Keep Astro. Use `ClientRouter` (view transitions)** so the persistent top nav and bottom nav don't flash between routes. Interactive pieces are React islands or small vanilla scripts. (Large decision: confirm.)
- **Routes** (decided with you):
  - `/` = Start page (every visit)
  - `/projects/[slug]` = home preview for that project; `/projects` redirects to the first. Switching icons updates the URL via a React island using `history.pushState`.
  - `/projects/[slug]/` case-study content lives on one page with scroll-snap sections (below).
  - `/about`
  - Open question for build time: whether the home preview and case-study body are the same route (preview = first snap section, "Open project" scrolls/snap to Deep dive) or two routes. **Recommended: same route**, the Overview *is* the home preview, so icon bar -> overview, "Open project" -> next section. (Matches "Overview buttons take the user to the marked section".)
- **Shortcuts**: one small `src/lib/shortcuts.ts` registry; bottom nav renders actions from a per-page config; each action = label, key glyph, handler. Ignore when focus is in inputs or with modifier keys.
- **Button press feel**: `:active { transform: scale(.97) }` plus shadow reduction (offset shadow collapses toward 0 to feel "pressed"), using existing `--media-frame-shadow`-style tokens, not Figma's. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. Use `motion` `press` only if CSS isn't enough.

## Phases (my suggested order differs slightly: foundation and cleanup first)
Each phase is a small, lintable, committable change. Phase 0-1 are the riskiest (touch the layout shell and delete content).

**Phase 0: Remove articles (⚠️ deletes files)**
Delete `src/pages/blog/*`, `src/layouts/BlogLayout.astro`, `src/content/blog/`, `src/pages/rss.xml.js`, `src/lib/categoryConfig.ts`, the `blog` collection in `src/content.config.ts`, category tokens in `global.css`, RSS link + `activeNav` in `BaseLayout.astro`, the "Writing" block in `index.astro`, and unused deps (`@astrojs/rss`, `@hugeicons/*`). Decide separately: orphaned `SubscribeForm.tsx` + `api/subscribe.ts` (recommend remove for now). Update README mentions.

**Phase 1: Foundation**
- Tokens (`global.css`): secondary button surface/ink/shadow, key-cap glyph chip, nav item states, pressed state. Both themes.
- `Button` secondary (extend `PillButton.astro` or a new `ActionButton.astro`), with key glyph slot, default / hover-focus / pressed / disabled states per Figma "New buttons".
- `TopNav.astro`: Projects / About (active state), live date-time (small script, `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, updates each minute, user's local time), GitHub / Discord / LinkedIn icons, sun/moon icon theme toggle (reuse existing view-transition toggle logic from `Footer.astro`). Remove `Footer.astro` and the `pt-16` hack.
- `BottomNav.astro` + `shortcuts.ts`. Hidden on Start and About.
- Enable `ClientRouter` in `BaseLayout`; make scripts safe across `astro:page-load`.

**Phase 2: Start page (`/`)**
Centered hero ("Hi there / I'm *Cody* [avatar]", Design Engineer / Rock Hill, SC / Version 2.0, social icons, Start button with Enter). `Enter` -> `/projects/ping` (first project). Reuse `/me-big-head-only.svg` and Redaction font. No top/bottom nav.

**Phase 3: Home / project preview**
- Icon bar (large icon buttons: Ping, Undercurrent, Watchtower, plus a disabled "Coming soon" tile as in Figma), selected one enlarged. Horizontal scroll with the selected item scrolled into view on small screens.
- Preview: "Project Ping" label, big Redaction headline with accent phrase (from `tagline`/`accentPhrase`), description, Type / Accessories / Role / Scope meta rows (extend project frontmatter: `type`, `accessories`).
- Motion: subtle entrance (fade/translate stagger, `motion` `animate`/`stagger`), cross-fade between projects, icon bar slide/scale. Basic first, polish after.
- Bottom nav actions: **Open project (Enter)**, **Watch walkthrough (W)**, **Back (Esc)** per Figma.

**Phase 4: Case study format (⚠️ largest change)**
- `ProjectLayout.astro` -> snap container (`scroll-snap-type: y proximity/mandatory`), sections: **Overview**, **Deep dive**, **Walkthrough**, **Gallery**. The "hump": a small overscroll/resistance zone at the end of the deep dive before snapping to the next section (CSS snap + an IntersectionObserver-driven short threshold; avoid hijacking wheel events unless proximity snapping can't deliver the feel; prototype this first).
- **Side nav** (`SubNav.astro`): Overview / Deep dive / Walkthrough / Gallery; Deep dive expands subitems (Intro, The problem, The solution, The approach, Examples, Postscript) only while active; scroll-spy via IntersectionObserver; click scrolls to section.
- **Deep dive**: reuse existing MDX content with new max width/layout. Reorder to Problem + Solution (combined, same section styling), then Approach (keep CSS dot-grid `::after` + `observeGridReveal`), then the detail `LabeledRow` blocks, then Postscript. Restyle text only; keep detail content in all 3 projects. Rename `.ping-section*` classes only if cheap.
- **Walkthrough**: Loom video (existing `loomUrl`) in-page. **Gallery**: collects existing images with captions.
- Bottom nav in case study: **Next project (X)**, **Back (Esc)** per Figma, plus section shortcuts.
- Overview: "larger than life" presentation reusing Phase 3 markup, with Motion entrance animations. Overview buttons jump to sections.
- Do Ping first end-to-end, then port Undercurrent and Watchtower (MDX restructure each).

**Phase 5: About page**
Hero ("Hi, I'm Cody" with gradient Cody + avatar), side nav (About me / How I work / Work history / Elsewhere), intro + facts rows, map, "How I work" numbered list, work history (Nexcess, USC Aiken) where project list items reuse the home list style and link to case studies, Elsewhere pills. Content is hard-coded in the Figma; store as a typed data module (`src/data/about.ts`).
- **Map**: start with your SVG as a static asset (I'll ask for it at this point). Later exploration: lo-fi dot-matrix map from real map data (e.g. MapLibre/OSM tiles rasterized to a dot grid on canvas). Separate follow-up.

**Phase 6: Responsive pass**
Best-effort small-screen behavior in each phase (icon bar scroll, side nav collapses to a horizontal/sticky bar or top select, bottom nav wraps/hides key glyphs on touch). Polish afterward.

## Critical files
- `src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro`, `ProjectLayout.astro`, `Footer.astro` (remove), new `TopNav.astro`, `BottomNav.astro`, `SubNav.astro`
- `src/styles/global.css` (tokens, button states, snap CSS)
- `src/pages/index.astro` (-> start), new `src/pages/projects/[slug].astro` rewrite, new `src/pages/about.astro`
- `src/content.config.ts`, `src/content/projects/*.mdx`
- `src/lib/animations.ts` (reuse `observeGridReveal`, `runFadeUpStagger`), new `src/lib/shortcuts.ts`
- Reuse: `PillButton.astro`, `LabeledRow`, `LightboxImage`, `LoopVideo`, `Postscript`, `projectIconMap.ts`, `MEDIA_FRAME_SHADOW`

## Verification (per phase)
- `bun run lint`, `bun run check` (astro check), `bun run format:check`, `bun run build` before each commit.
- `bun run dev`, then check in the built-in browser at desktop and mobile widths, in both themes: nav active states, clock ticking, theme toggle, keyboard shortcuts (Enter / W / X / Esc), icon switching + URL/Back, scroll-snap + hump, side-nav scroll-spy and expansion, overview jump buttons, reduced-motion.
- Compare each page against Figma screenshots (frame ids above).
- Remember: no existing tests; add none unless you want them.

## Notes / warnings
- Small, incremental commits, one phase at a time; I'll pause for your confirmation before Phases 0, 1 and 4.
- Pre-existing nits to fix in passing: Watchtower opener alt text says "Undercurrent"; README mentions a nonexistent `src/assets/`.
